comment: THE DEAD-EXPORT FENCE baseline. An export listed here is exported by a LIVE file but has NO live caller — and a TEST IS NEVER A CALLER. A CALLER is: a code reference in another live module; an intra-module reference (definition + >=1 real call, e.g. completeTaskPlan -> completeExecution inside actions.js); a CALL in a shipped instruction surface — the name invoked as name( or referenced as require('./x').name; or a declared export root. A BARE PROSE TOKEN (even a backtick code-span that merely NAMES the function) and COMMENTS are NOT callers — a citation is not an invocation. RATCHET: maxDead may only ever be LOWERED and entries only ever REMOVED (by wiring or deleting). RE-SEED 2026-07-19 — COUPLED MOVEMENT, NOT A CODE CHANGE: the FILE fence was tightened to the same caller rule this fence has always used (a presence-check array of path literals is no longer a call edge; a path merely NAMED in markdown prose is no longer an execution root). analyzeExports classifies exports only INSIDE LIVE FILES, so shrinking the live set mechanically moved this count: 102 -> 71. 34 entries LEFT the list because their whole FILE is now reported unreachable and a dead export inside an already-dead file is the FILE fence's business (reporting both would double-count the same defect) — every one of them is still dead, now tracked one level up in .ctoc/reachability-baseline.json. 3 entries JOINED it, and they are DEAD BY TRANSITIVITY, not new defects: src/lib/actions.js#deletePlan was credited only by src/lib/stale-cleanup.js, src/lib/inbox.js#createQuestion only by the eu-ai-act/gdpr agent runners, and src/lib/regulatory-regime.js#retentionDays only by src/lib/retention.js — every one of those creditors is itself now reported unreachable, so the credit was a dead file vouching for an export. Their host files are live; their callers are not. RE-SEED PROVENANCE (R4-C, 2026-07-14, kept): R4-B credited any identifier inside a FENCED code block, which buried 23 genuinely-reachable exports that CTOC recipes invoke with INLINE code — including approveSubplans (the Gate-3 done-all gate) — and falsely credited src/lib/ui.js#doctor via unrelated fenced tokens; call syntax replaced fenced-block membership. R6-C: src/lib/ui.js#doctor RESOLVED by DELETION. | RATCHET DOWN 71 -> 69 (2026-07-19, MEASURED live from analyzeExports, not predicted): src/lib/iron-loop.js#validateForTodo and #generateIronLoopTemplate were DELETED, not wired. validateForTodo had a Gate-2-sounding name, zero callers, and tested for the marker "## Execution Steps (Iron Loop 8-16)" which this module never writes (generateExecutionPlan emits "## Execution Plan (Steps 8-16)"), so it rejected every plan the module itself produced — a broken predicate with an authoritative name is an invitation for a future caller to trust it. The deletion cascaded to hasIronLoopSteps and IRON_LOOP_MARKER, which were used only by each other and by tests, and a test is never a caller. | RATCHET DOWN 69 -> 68 (2026-07-20, MEASURED live from analyzeExports, not predicted): src/lib/ui.js#adminDashboard was DELETED, not wired, together with dashboard, progress, blocked and getPhase — five screen builders whose only callers were their own tests. The other four were never on this list, and WHY NOT is a finding about this fence rather than a fact about that code: analyzeExports credits an export when any LIVE MODULE MENTIONS ITS NAME as a bare identifier token, and dashboard/progress/blocked are ordinary English words appearing in unrelated live modules. That is the same "a citation is not an invocation" defect the FILE fence was rebuilt to remove on 2026-07-19, still live in the EXPORT path — it under-reports dead code, and it will keep silently crediting any generically-named dead export. Not fixed here (src/lib/reachability.js was out of that slice scope); see plan 00153 for the mechanism and the proposed fix. The deletion cascaded ONE level: src/lib/state-manager.js#STEP_DESCRIPTIONS had exactly one live reader, progress() in ui.js, so removing progress orphaned it and it was DELETED too rather than added here — a new entry is forbidden, and keeping a dead require() so this fence still saw the token would have been gaming the instrument. STEP_NAMES is untouched and still live via both hooks. | RATCHET DOWN 68 -> 66 (2026-07-28, plan 00187, MEASURED live from analyzeExports, not predicted): COUPLED MOVEMENT again, the mirror image of the 2026-07-19 reseed. Plan 00187 fixed the FILE fence to see a require WITHOUT a file extension (Node resolves require('./x') to ./x.js) and widened the skills walk to every .md, not only SKILL.md. Two consequences reached THIS fence, both legitimate and both the tighter direction: (1) src/lib/actions.js#deletePlan LEFT because its sole creditor src/lib/stale-cleanup.js — which the 2026-07-19 comment above names as the only file that credited it — is REACHABLE again (start.md's cleanup-exec recipe runs it via require('{{CTOC_ROOT}}/src/lib/stale-cleanup'), an extensionless require the file fence now sees). A dead file vouching for an export became a LIVE file vouching for it; the coupling this baseline already recorded simply ran in reverse. NOTE the credit is by bare token (stale-cleanup.js defines its OWN deletePlan) — the same generically-named-token coarseness the 2026-07-20 note flags as still-live in this fence and defers to plan 00153; it is not introduced here. (2) src/lib/inbox.js#createQuestion LEFT because skills/agent-fragments/async-choice-protocol.md is now a scanned surface and it CALLS createQuestion() with parens — SURFACE_CALL_RE credits name( as a call, so a shipped fragment instructing the session to call createQuestion() is a caller. Plan 00187's own text predicted this would STAY dead as prose; that prediction was about the FILE fence (inbox.js does not become a file root) and was wrong about THIS fence, whose call-syntax rule credits the parenthesized call. Neither removal changes fence semantics; both are measured facts absorbed as the reward ratchet.
